transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-11-05 09:23 PST; Duration: ~46 minutes; Platform: Zoom; Recording ID: ff-20271105-0923.
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (BrightFind - Head of Search), Priya Nair (BrightFind - Eng Manager), Diego Alvarez (BrightFind - Platform Eng).

Summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking flow for BrightFind search relevance use-case. Demo showed embeddings generation, neighborhood search, and Redwood's rerank endpoint that uses context + embedding features. Discussed SLAs, latency vs cost tradeoffs, and compliance (SOC2, KMS). Agreed to run a 1M-query rerank POC on hosted infra and to share security docs.

Topics: Hosted embeddings endpoint, vector storage options, rerank endpoint (score + explainability), batching, latency/cost knobs, caching (prefix/KV cache), security (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), POC logistics.

Action items (from call): see metadata above.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm with Maya who is our solutions engineer, we'll do a quick walkthrough on embeddings and rerank and then leave time for Q&A.
[00:12] Liam: Hey thanks, appreciate it. Quick note, we only have ~45 minutes so if we could prioritize the rerank flow that'd be great.
[00:18] Maya: Yep totally. Quick agenda - first a 10 minute primer on the hosted embeddings endpoint, then a demo of a retrieval + rerank pipeline, then discuss perf numbers and POC next steps. Sound good?
[00:30] Priya: Sounds good. Also, need to know if we can keep data in our EU region (data residency) and whether we can use our KMS.
[00:36] Jordan: Yep that's on the table — we have region pinning for hosted and KMS integration for enterprise customers, we'll share the security pack after. Maya will show where that plugs in.
[00:45] Maya: Ok jumping in — so embeddings endpoint is a simple REST call, you pass text or batches of texts, we return fixed-dim vectors. We also support streaming embedding ops for large uploads. Here is an example request, note the batch param and the model selector.
[01:05] Maya: For BrightFind, given you have a mix of short queries and long docs, we'd recommend a 1024-d embedding model variant that gives a good tradeoff of accuracy vs token cost.
[01:18] Diego: Quick question — we currently store vectors in OpenSearch. Does Redwood require using a specific vector DB or can we keep OpenSearch?
[01:25] Maya: You can keep OpenSearch, Pinecone, or any vector store — we return embeddings and scores, and the rerank endpoint can accept candidate docs with precomputed embeddings or raw text. Many customers keep storage in OpenSearch and call Redwood for scoring.
[01:40] Liam: When you say rerank endpoint, is that another API call where we pass candidate IDs + context?
[01:46] Maya: Exactly. Rerank is a synchronous endpoint: you pass the query, candidate list (optionally with embeddings), and it returns a ranked list with scores and an explanatory field. Behind the scenes we combine semantic similarity signals with model-based cross-encoders, and we have tuning knobs for latency vs accuracy.
[02:05] Priya: What sort of latency are we talking about for a 10-candidate rerank? Our SLO is 150 ms median for search.
[02:12] Maya: On hosted, for a 10-candidate rerank we typically see 60–180 ms depending on model—if you want 95th percentile tightness we can switch to a faster quantized model or use prefix cache. For example our 1024-d configuration with quantized inference is ~80 ms p50 and ~160 ms p95 in us-west under moderate load.
[02:34] Liam: That's promising. Cost wise, how does that compare to running everything in-house? We currently run heavy query volume—about 500k queries/day.
[02:42] Jordan: Cost comparison depends on many factors — token volume, embedding dimension, caching hit rate. In hosted mode you pay per-embedding and per-rerank call; Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and caching to reduce unit costs. We'll send a cost model spreadsheet after this call.
[03:00] Diego: Are there size limits for candidate lists? We sometimes do larger candidate sets for long-tail queries.
[03:06] Maya: API supports variable candidate counts; for large candidate sets we recommend doing a cheap vector similarity filter first and then run rerank on top-K. For super large jobs we can also suggest a batched rerank flow to amortize overhead.
[03:22] Liam: Can we do the rerank off of precomputed pairwise features? Like clicks + recency metrics?
[03:27] Maya: Yes you can include custom features per candidate and the rerank model will combine them. We accept numeric feature arrays and categorical signals in the payload.
[03:36] Priya: On the security side — SOC2, SSO, audit logs, and key management — what's supported for hosted customers?
[03:44] Jordan: Hosted supports SOC2 compliance, SAML SSO, fine-grained RBAC via our Console, and customer-managed KMS for enterprise tiers. We'll attach the SOC2 report and the network architecture doc.
[03:58] Diego: Does hosted keep any raw text from rerank requests? Our compliance team is strict about retention.
[04:04] Maya: By default we retain logs for 30 days for monitoring but you can opt into zero-retention for request payloads and we can set up a private deployment or dedicated capacity if required. We'll note that in the security pack.
[04:18] Liam: Ok good. Let's see the demo flow.
[04:22] Maya: Switching to my screen — here's the Console quickstart. But I'll demo the API using curl for embeddings then a small Python snippet for rerank.
[04:30] [Screen shared: terminal with sample curl]
[04:34] Maya: First call — POST /v1/embeddings with a small batch. Response returns vector and model metadata. Note the "model_version" field — you can pin versions for consistent results.
[04:50] Liam: Are embeddings deterministic across calls? We need stable vectors for indexing.
[04:55] Maya: Yes for a pinned model version embeddings are deterministic; different model variants obviously differ. If you re-embed with a newer version you'll see drift.
[05:05] Maya: Now I show candidate retrieval from OpenSearch — here I run a vector query to get top 200, then call Redwood rerank with top 20.
[05:15] [00:05:15] Priya: There's a slight audio cut but we see the code.
[05:20] Maya: On the rerank request we pass query text, top candidates as object with id, text, precomputed_embedding, and features. Here's the JSON payload sample.
[05:30] Maya: Sending the rerank call... got response. Results show reordered IDs with scores and an explain field that highlights why doc B scored higher (term match + semantic).
[05:45] Liam: That explainability is useful for product. Is the explain string generated by the model?
[05:50] Maya: It's a model-generated snippet combined with signal attribution (we surface which features pushed the score up). It's not a formal proof but it's good for triage.
[06:05] Diego: For evaluation, can we run a rerank compare between your reranker and our baseline? How do we instrument that?
[06:12] Maya: Yes, for POC we usually run A/B-style offline evals. We provide a notebook that takes your labeled relevance judgments and computes NDCG/recall and can call the rerank endpoint in batch. We'll share that notebook.
[06:25] Liam: Great. Next, how does batching work for embeddings? We sometimes ingest millions of docs.
[06:33] Maya: We expose a bulk embeddings endpoint and streaming clients. Also support chunked uploads to S3 with a background ingestion job. For very large corpora we recommend using our bulk ingestion + async indexing; team will help size the batch windows.
[06:46] Priya: Any best practices on embedding dimension vs search quality?
[06:50] Maya: Higher dims (1024/2048) give better semantic fidelity but cost more and increase vector DB size. For most e-commerce search 512/1024 is good. We'll recommend 1024 for BrightFind given your mixed content.
[07:02] Liam: What about caching — you mentioned prefix/KV cache earlier?
[07:07] Maya: Yes our runtime supports prefix and KV cache — for chat it's prefix caching, for search rerank we cache embeddings and cheap similarity results to reduce redundant computation. Cache hit rates are workload dependent; Optimize can run a simulation and estimate savings.
[07:20] Diego: On infra — is the hosted runtime multi-tenant or dedicated per account? We need strong isolation for some datasets.
[07:27] Jordan: Hosted is multi-tenant with logical isolation; for stricter isolation you can choose Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or Private deployment. Many teams start on hosted and then move to Dedicated as they scale.
[07:40] Priya: If we start hosted and later move to Dedicated, is the API surface identical?
[07:44] Maya: Yes same API/Console and same rollout controls — that’s one of Redwood's selling points.
[07:52] Liam: For the POC we want to run a 1M query rerank test on a subset of live traffic — do you support traffic shadowing?
[07:58] Maya: Yes we support shadowing and can help set up a traffic sample. For 1M queries we can advise on throughput and provide a dedicated POC slot to avoid noisy neighbors.
[08:10] Liam: Nice. Regarding cost, if we do shadowing at full qps, are there overage protections?
[08:15] Jordan: We support quota limits and rate-limiting and can set a POC cap. We'll include pricing tiers in the doc.
[08:24] [08:24] Priya: Any integrations with our current observability stack? We use Datadog and Sentry.
[08:29] Maya: We export request/latency metrics and traces and you can ingest them into Datadog; we also push audit logs to your syslog or S3 for long-term retention.
[08:40] Diego: Do you have any guarantees around SLA in hosted? We need to understand recovery and fallback if an endpoint is slow.
[08:47] Jordan: Hosted has best-effort SLAs; Dedicated has an SLA-backed offering. We also have automated fallback policies that will route to cheaper model variants or alternate regions to maintain availability.
[09:00] Liam: Ok good. A couple more technical ones — do you support quantized models for rerank and what's the impact on accuracy?
[09:06] Maya: Yes, we have quantized variants. Typically accuracy drops are small for classification/ranking but it depends on your eval set. That's why we recommend running the same eval notebook on both float and quantized models to measure NDCG delta.
[09:20] Priya: For HIPAA-like constraints, is there an on-prem option?
[09:24] Jordan: Yes Private deployment is available (VPC and on-prem packaged installers). That comes with a licensing and support contract.
[09:31] Liam: Can you walk through an example rerank payload with features?
[09:36] Maya: Sure — here's JSON: {query:..., candidates:[{id, text, embedding, features:{clicks, recency}}]}. We'll redact the full example in shared notebook.
[09:52] Priya: Are there rate limits per-tenant?
[09:55] Jordan: Yes, and you can request increases. For POC we'll set permissive limits and then dial them for production.
[10:05] Liam: For evaluation metrics — you mentioned NDCG, recall, and a custom business metric we use called "session success".
[10:12] Maya: We can plug in custom metrics into the eval notebook; Optimize can run periodic regression monitoring against baseline prompts.
[10:20] Diego: One more infra detail — can we point Redwood to our VPC for egress?
[10:25] Maya: For private deployments and some dedicated setups we can peer into your VPC or deploy within your VPC in cloud providers; hosted is routed through Redwood's network but we support VPC peering for enterprise.
[10:38] Liam: Ok great. Moving towards POC logistics, what do you need from us?
[10:42] Maya: We'll need a sample dataset (S3 path preferred), labels or relevance judgments, an example of current retrieval pipeline (OpenSearch query), and a point-of-contact for infra to set up shadowing.
[10:55] Jordan: We'll prepare the POC runbook and share next steps. Proposed timeline: kick off next week, 2-week run, then a results review.
[11:05] Priya: Internal stakeholders — legal will request the SOC2 and the DPA, security will want the network diagram.
[11:12] Jordan: We'll bundle those.
[11:16] Maya: Quick demo wrap — here's a side-by-side NDCG chart from a prior customer where rerank improved NDCG@10 by ~12% after tuning. Your results will vary, but it's illustrative.
[11:32] Liam: That helps. One question — can rerank also surface reranking reasons to end-users? We're thinking of showing a "Why this result" overlay in UI.
[11:40] Maya: You can surface the explain snippet, which is short and can be sanitized; we recommend a governance step to control what messages reach customers.
[11:50] Diego: Any caveats about long-tail queries and cold-start docs?
[11:55] Maya: Cold-start docs benefit from hybrid signals — add metadata + recency signals as features; that helps the reranker generalize.
[12:05] Liam: Ok let's get to the security bits — Maya can you summarize what's in the SOC2 pack?
[12:10] Maya: It includes our SOC2 report, DPA template, network diagram, KMS integration guide, and audit log examples. We'll redact some internal ops bits but the core compliance artifacts are included.
[12:25] Priya: Will you be able to sign our DPA?
[12:28] Jordan: Yes we sign the standard DPA; legal will coordinate.
[12:32] Liam: Great. Any final performance tuning tips?
[12:36] Maya: Use caching for stable queries, use a smaller candidate set for real-time rerank, and batch embeddings in ingestion. Also consider mixed-precision models for lower latency.
[12:50] Priya: Ok that's helpful.
[13:00] Jordan: Quick recap — action items: Jordan sends pricing + POC runbook; Maya sends SOC2 + notebook; BrightFind to provide dataset and POC point-of-contact. We'll schedule the POC kickoff for next week.
[13:14] Liam: Sounds good. Thanks both.
[13:18] Maya: Thanks team. We'll follow up in email.
[13:22] [Call ends - 09:23 to 10:09 PST ~46 minutes]

Notes on transcript quality: Automated transcript had a few mis-heard words: "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "KV cash", product names like "Redwood Dedicated" occasionally as "Redwood dedicate". Speakers occasionally overlap and speaker labels are split between first names and generic labels in some timestamps.
